title: Fujitsu iRMC S6 02.63S C0/D0 OEM handler audit

statusDefinition.direct: Entry handler's wire shape and primary effect are statically established; dependent backend semantics or live rack behavior may still be unknown.
statusDefinition.partial: Handler exists but a delegated backend, complex selector, or opaque field prevents full wire contract.
statusDefinition.opaque: No handler body or contract recovered; zero entries in these two families.

limitations: Static analysis only for this artifact; no payloads were sent to the BMC.
Registration privilege is Admin, but effective RMCP+ reachability and rack activation require separate live evidence.
Temporary /tmp decompilation paths are reproducible from source table Ghidra addresses; the pinned firmware library is the durable evidence.

highRisk.finding: Restore parameter page-zero path can copy 24 bytes from request+8 after checking only total request length >8; the direct total<=24 path also passes unvalidated request+8 length to backend. Out-of-bounds read candidate with configuration mutation.
HSS setter copies declared data length from request+3 after only checking request length >=4; out-of-bounds read candidate, blade gated.
Flash status reset reads selector and can call tflashSetStatus even after recording C9 for malformed length.
Shared image-name setter calls strlen(request+1) on fixed 32-byte request before guaranteed terminator; out-of-bounds read candidate.
Mode 4 uses request byte 7 as runtime-array index without visible local bound check; potential memory corruption, static only.
Boot-option setter writes two bytes without a local request-length check and returns CC00 despite backend write failure, blade gated.
Any request longer than one byte causes an unconditional 20-byte memcpy from request+1, so a two-byte request can read beyond its supplied payload; mode-zero reads also reset throttling averages.
ASRR setter interprets bitmask-selected offsets through byte 11 without comprehensive request-length checks; earlier fields can be committed before a later validation or backend error.

Shared TFTP setter validates address text with inet_pton without requiring a terminator in the 31-byte payload; selector 2 can append up to 30 bytes to a 64-byte stored value in a 72-byte local buffer without a combined-length check.

SSO session reservation accepts caller-provided requested privileges and user/path fields, then returns a 24-byte session material block; session-based transports mask privilege bits, while non-session/IPMB behavior differs. Treat output as credential-sensitive.
